jobs.occupation: Interdisciplinary Postdoctoral Fellow in Host-Directed Antimicrobial Research
jobs.description:
We are looking for a highly motivated and dynamic postdoc for a one-year position to commence 1 March 2027 or after agreement.

  Introduction

  Antimicrobial resistance is a growing global health challenge that highlights the need for innovative therapeutic strategies beyond conventional antibiotic treatment.

  Host-directed antimicrobial strategies are attracting increasing interest as complementary approaches to conventional antimicrobial therapy. Recent studies have demonstrated that a novel synthetic compound improves survival in methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA)-infected Caenorhabditis elegans. Furthermore, previous studies in mammalian cells suggest that the compound may exert immunomodulatory effects, raising the possibility that stimulation of host defence pathways contributes to protection against infection.

  This project aims to determine whether the novel synthetic compound can stimulate innate immunity and enhance host defence pathways in C. elegans and thereby contribute to protection against MRSA-infection. Using a combination of immunology, microbiology, and transcriptomics, the successful candidate will lead the experimental investigation of the phenotypic and transcriptional responses underlying this protective effect. All experimental work will be conducted in C. elegans.

  Required qualifications

   	
• A PhD in immunology, infection biology, microbiology, molecular biology, biomedical sciences, pharmacology, or a related discipline. 	
• Hands-on experience with the maintenance and experimental use of Caenorhabditis elegans, preferably as an infection model. 	
• Knowledge to innate immunity and host defence pathways. 	
• Demonstrated ability to conduct independent research. 	
• Excellent written and oral communication skills in English.   Highly desirable qualifications

   	
• Knowledge to innate immunity and host defence pathways in Caenorhabditis elegans. 	
• Experience with bacterial culture and experimental microbiology. 	
• Experience with omics-data analysis (such as RNA-seq data). 	
• Experience with quantitative PCR (qPCR) and gene expression analysis. 	
• Experience with RNA interference (RNAi) and gene-silencing approaches. 	
• Knowledge of antimicrobial compounds and antimicrobial resistance. 	
• Experience contributing to external funding applications. 	
• A strong publication record relative to career stage.   Key responsibilities

  The postdoctoral fellow will conduct research within host-directed antimicrobial strategies and innate immunity. The successful candidate is expected to contribute to student supervision, assist in the preparation of external funding applications, and lead the dissemination of research findings through scientific publications and presentations, as well as participate in other academic activities.

  Research environment and collaboration 

  The successful candidate will be based in a research environment with expertise in C. elegans biology and will interact closely with collaborators possessing complementary expertise in immunity, microbiology, and bioinformatics. The interdisciplinary nature of the project provides excellent opportunities for scientific exchange and the development of skills across multiple disciplines while independently driving the research project.

  Further information

  Further information on the Department is linked at https://ivh.ku.dk/. Inquiries about the position can be made to Associate Professor Tina V. A. Hansen, alstrup@sund.ku.dk

  Starting date and duration

  The position is available from 1 March 2027 or after agreement. The position is a fixed-term, full-time postdoctoral appointment for a period of one year.

  Terms of employment

  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  The application, in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include 

   	
• Curriculum vitae 	
• Diplomas (Master and PhD degree or equivalent) 	
• Research plan – description of current and future research plans 	
• Complete publication list 	
• Separate reprints of 3 particularly relevant papers 	
• Contact information for 2–3 references.   The deadline for applications is Tuesday 24 November 2026, 23:59pm CET

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment work has been completed each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself.

  You can read about the recruitment process at https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

  Interviews are expected to be held in weeks 2-4, 2027.

  The University of Copenhagen wish to reflect the diversity of society and encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of personal background.

jobs.description:

jobs.occupation: Assistant Professorship in Anthropology, Aarhus University

jobs.description:
The Department of Anthropology, School of Culture and Society, invites applications for a three-year position as assistant professor in relation to the research project “Stories from my new life: Mobile transitions and social becomings among resettled refugees in Denmark” (TRANSIT).

An assistant professorship is a full-time, three-year training position that involves research and teaching at the BA and MA level and includes an obligatory course in university teaching for assistant professors. The position will commence on 1 February, 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. 

Place of employment: Department of Anthropology, Moesgaard Allé 20, 8270 Højbjerg, Denmark.

The Faculty of Arts is committed to creating an inclusive working environment and therefore encourages all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of personal background, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, ethnicity etc.

The position
The position will be associated with the research project TRANSIT at the Department of Anthropology and is a combined teaching and research position.

Here is a brief description of the TRANSIT project:

In 2021-2024 app. 600 Congolese women and children were resettled in Denmark under the UNHCR resettlement program. TRANSIT is concerned with resettled refugees’ life transitions, understood as a set of complex legal, social and existential transitions that are particularly urgent in the context of resettlement: 1) the transition from youth to adulthood; 2) the transition from being single to being married; and 3) the transition into old age and, ultimately, death. The project aims to establish a collaboration between Aarhus University, VIVE – The Danish Center for Social Science Research, FLUGT – Refugee Museum of Denmark, DFUNK – Dansk Flygtningehjælp Ungdom and a large group of resettled families in order to: a) create a mobile pop-up exhibition to be presented across Denmark in 2029; b) develop research-based teaching materials for pupils in the final years of Folkeskolen and in Gymnasiet on what it means to be resettled and start a new life in Denmark; and c) publish articles in leading peer-reviewed journals – based on a range of qualitative and quantitative data – on storytelling and life transitions following resettlement.

The selected candidate is expected to do individual fieldwork, be main responsible for a work-package (developing research-based teaching material with FLUGT – Refugee Museum of Denmark), and to be a dedicated member of the project team and engaged in all the project activities and responsibilities.

The position is offered with a view to attracting qualified applicants with an established and well-documented research record in innovative and internationally recognized research within anthropology and a specialization in migration and refugee studies, collaborative methods and creative forms of research dissemination. 

Research
The selected applicant will be expected to contribute to core activities at the School of Culture and Society and Aarhus University in general and contribute to the Department of Anthropology’s research activities and output in particular. They will be expected to take an interest in interdisciplinary research collaboration within the Department of Anthropology, the School of Culture and Society, the Faculty of Arts, and beyond. 

The selected applicant will also be expected to develop new research projects with internal and external partners and to raise external research funding. The applicant’s research credentials and publication record within the field, e.g. anthropology, migration and refugee studies, collaborative methods and creative forms of research dissemination, will be assessed not just on existing publications and other research contributions but also on research potential.

Past research output will be assessed based on the active research time of the applicant in question. We therefore ask applicants to specify any career breaks they have had (for instance due to maternity/paternity leave or sick leave) so we may discount these periods when assessing research productivity.

Teaching
The position will involve some teaching (up to 33% of the time) as agreed upon with the Head of the Department and the project PI. The selected applicant will be required to teach and supervise at BA and MA levels of the department’s degree programs in Anthropology and Human Security and will be expected to have teaching experience at university level. 

We emphasise the importance of maintaining a professional and respectful relationship between staff and students, so applicants should be able to demonstrate and exemplify their commitment to participatory teaching initiatives and student involvement as part of their teaching portfolio.

Qualifications
Applicants must hold a PhD or equivalent qualifications in anthropology or a related discipline. They must also be able to document the following: 

• An internationally oriented research profile documented through relevant academic publications, and possibly other research contributions, at the international level
• Experience of university-level teaching and a commitment to teaching development and the supervision of student projects
• Experience of or interest in active participation in international research collaboration
• Experience of or interest in obtaining external research funding
• Experience of or interest in research dessimination for a non-academic audience
Applicants are asked to submit:

• A concise statement of motivation for applying for the position, including a description of experience with public research dessimination (maximum two pages).
• A full CV (one page).
• A full publication list (research outputs and public dissemination)
• A maximum of two publications.
Only submitted publications will be assessed; a list of publications is not sufficient. As a result, applications without submitted publications will not be assessed.

References or recommendations should not be included with the application. Applicants who are selected for a job interview may be asked to provide professional references.

Language and further information
Applicants can teach and supervise in English at university level.

If the selected applicant is not fluent in Danish, they will be expected to acquire the language within a period of approximately two years. 

To maintain and develop the department’s research environment, the person appointed is expected to be present at the department on a regular basis.

Applications must be uploaded in English.

For further information about the TRANSIT project (including the project description), please contact, PI, Professor Mikkel Rytter, mikkel.rytter@cas.au.dk

For further information about the application procedure, please contact Human Resources: iks-hr-sag@au.dk.

Knowledge exchange
It is expected that the selected applicant will engage in knowledge exchange as described in the strategy for the Faculty of Arts Strategy Arts 2020-2025 (au.dk), for instance research cooperation with private companies, government consultancy, cooperation with civil society partners or the public dissemination of knowledge. Applicants should document any prior experience within the field of knowledge exchange.

School of Culture and Society
The School of Culture and Society is a vibrant research community engaged in understanding the cultural and social conditions that shape human life. Our work examines how people interact with their environments, from prehistory to the present and across both local and global contexts. Through cross-sector and cross-disciplinary partnerships, we aim to support research innovation and contribute to addressing the major questions facing society. In both research and education, we are committed to bringing the humanities into active dialogue with partners beyond the university.

The School is committed to:

• Promoting an international environment characterized by active academic and interdisciplinary collaboration.
• Encouraging innovative and experimental approaches to research, teaching, and communication.
• Cultivating environments that generate new knowledge and educate students for the future.
• Advancing broad engagement with digital humanities.
• Upholding a deep commitment to addressing both local and global societal challenges.
• Creating an inclusive, diverse, and sustainable workplace and organization.
Read more about the school here School of Culture and Society - Aarhus University

International applicants
International applicants are encouraged to check Family and work-life balance in Denmark (au.dk) and Attractive working conditions (au.dk) for further information about the benefits of working at Aarhus University and in Denmark, including healthcare, paid holidays and, if relevant, maternity/paternity leave, childcare and schooling. Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including a Relocation and onboarding services for international AU staff and career counselling for expat partners. For information about taxation, see Taxation aspects of international researchers’ employment by AU.

Qualification requirements
Applicants should hold a PhD or equivalent academic qualifications.

Formalities

• Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.
• Further information on the application and supplementary materials may be found in Application Guidelines.
• The application must outline the applicant's motivation for applying for the position, attaching a curriculum vitae, a teaching portfolio, a complete list of published works, a research plan, copies of degree certificates and examples of academic production (mandatory, but no more than two examples). Please upload this material electronically along with your application. Please note that although the application process can be completed in the Aarhus University system without up-loading publications or a teaching portfolio, applications that do not include uploaded publications as well as a teaching portfolio (or equivalent documentation of teaching experience and qualifications) will not be considered.
If nothing else is noted, applications must be submitted in English. Application deadline is at 11.59 pm Danish time (same as Central European Time) on the deadline day.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Shortlists may be prepared with the candidates that have been selected for a detailed academic assessment. A committee set up by the head of school is responsible for selecting the most qualified candidates. See this link for further information about shortlisting at the Faculty of Arts:  shortlisting

Terms of employment
• Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations.
Salary and terms of employment are governed by the Cirkulære om overenskomst for akademikere i staten  (in Danish). You will be employed as Assistant Professorship at base pay level 4–8 with additional supplements in accordance with the Cirkulære om protokollat om visse ansættelsesvilkår for videnskabeligt personale ved universiteter (in Danish).

The job content and qualification requirements are described in further detail in the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

About Arts
The Faculty of Arts is one of Northern Europe’s most significant faculties for research and higher education in the humanities, theology and education. Within this broad academic scope, the faculty comprises approximately 700 researchers, 200 PhD students, 9,000 Bachelor’s and Master’s degree students, and 1,500 further and continuing education students. We believe that the best ideas arise when different perspectives meet – and that research, teaching and innovation are best developed in dialogue with the surrounding society.

jobs.occupation: Mechanical Design Engineer
jobs.description:
Mechanical Design Engineer: Develop robust medical devices from concept to production

Would you like to use your mechanical engineering expertise to develop medical devices that make a real difference for people with intimate healthcare needs?

Working with engineers, scientists and project managers, you will turn product requirements and concepts into robust mechanical solutions, combining creative problem-solving with engineering rigour from concept evaluation through to production.

Welcome to CC & BC Mechanical Engineering

At our headquarters in Humlebæk, Denmark, you will join CC & BC Mechanical Engineering within Product Development, developing products for Continence Care and Bowel Care.

Mechanical design connects what users need with how a product performs and how reliably it can be manufactured. Our work brings together functionality, materials, tolerances and production considerations to create practical solutions that perform consistently in everyday use.

You will work closely with colleagues across Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Design, Technical Design, Materials, Systems Engineering, Usability and Test Engineering, as well as Manufacturing Systems Development and Centre of Excellence specialists.

Turn product concepts into reliable, manufacturable solutions

As our new Mechanical Design Engineer, you will plan and deliver mechanical design activities in Product Development projects. Your work will span concept development and evaluation, detailed design, verification support and transfer to production.

You will take ownership of your mechanical deliverables and provide clear technical conclusions and recommendations. Working within the agreed project scope, you will identify risks early, make design trade-offs visible and bring in the right expertise to move decisions forward.

More specifically, you will:

•    Develop and evaluate mechanical concepts, translating product requirements into practical design solutions in collaboration with Systems Engineering and relevant specialists.

•    Develop and document mechanical designs using 3D CAD, working closely with Technical Design on drawings and specifications.

•    Apply robust design methods and tolerance analysis to understand variation and secure reliable product performance.

•    Apply Design for X principles to balance performance, manufacturability, sustainability and cost, involving manufacturing specialists early.

•    Use calculations, simulation, prototypes and test evidence to evaluate solutions and support timely design decisions.

•    Contribute mechanical expertise to risk assessments, verification planning, technical reviews and design documentation.

•    Plan and deliver your activities against agreed project commitments, communicating risks, dependencies and the impact of proposed changes early.

•    Share technical learning and help improve mechanical design practices across projects.

A mechanical engineer with practical judgement and a collaborative approach

You enjoy both exploring concepts and working through the details that make a design reliable. You can turn analysis into clear recommendations, explain design trade-offs and challenge unclear assumptions constructively.

You take a structured approach without making solutions more complex than necessary. You understand when further analysis is needed and when the available evidence supports moving forward. Above all, you take responsibility for your work while recognising that strong product solutions depend on contributions from several disciplines.

We imagine that you:

•    Hold a BSc or MSc in mechanical engineering, mechanical design, product development or a related discipline.

•    Have experience developing mechanical solutions, including plastic components for injection moulding and high-volume production.

•    Work confidently with 3D CAD, preferably SolidWorks.

•    Have experience with robust design, tolerance calculations and design for manufacture.

•    Can apply engineering theory, calculations and data analysis to practical design challenges.

•    Communicate technical ideas and conclusions clearly, both visually and verbally.

•    Work effectively across disciplines and document your work clearly.

•    Communicate confidently in English.

Experience in medical devices or another regulated industry is an advantage. We also value experience with simulation and an interest in using digital tools, including AI where relevant, to improve engineering analysis and development efficiency.

You do not need to know every method from the outset. Curiosity, sound engineering judgement and a willingness to develop your expertise are important.

Interested?

If you would like to know more about the position, please contact Jesper Bruun Jensen, Head of Continence Care & Bowel Care Mechanical Engineering, at DKJBRJ@coloplast.com.

We review applications continuously, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. The position will remain open until a suitable candidate has been found.

Pursuing an ambitious growth agenda, Coloplast develops and markets products and services that make life easier for people with intimate healthcare needs. Employing about 16.000 people and with products available in more than 143 countries, we are one of the world´s leading medical device companies. jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship in antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) engineering: internalization and lysosomal delivery
jobs.description:
Biotech Research and Innovation Centre (BRIC) / Finsen Laboratory, Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen

  A 3-year PhD fellowship is available in the research group of Associate Professor Lars Henning Engelholm. Expected start: 15 January 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

   

  The project

  Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) depend on efficient internalization and lysosomal processing to release their cytotoxic payload. Inefficient trafficking limits potency and restricts current ADCs to targets with very high receptor density. The PhD project will engineer and test next-generation ADCs with improved internalization and lysosomal routing. This includes bispecific constructs that combine our established ADC targets (uPAR, MMP14, uPARAP and the Mannose Receptor) with receptors that drive lysosomal delivery, such as IGF2R. Lead candidates will be evaluated in cancer cell models and in vivo, including models of sarcoma and glioblastoma.

  The project is part of the Novo Nordisk Foundation Distinguished Innovator project "Breaking Barriers: Engineering ADCs for Efficient BBB Transport and Lysosomal Targeting", in collaboration with Professor Matthias Herth (Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, UCPH) and Professor Katrine Qvortrup (Department of Chemistry, DTU).

   

  Main tasks

   	
•  	Production, purification and validation of recombinant and bispecific antibodies

 	 	
•  	Conjugation of antibodies to cytotoxic payloads and characterization of the resulting ADCs

 	 	
•  	Cell-based assays: antibody uptake and internalization, flow cytometry, drug screening and cytotoxicity/cell viability assays

 	 	
•  	In vivo efficacy studies of ADC candidates in tumor models

 	 	
•  	Writing scientific publications and presenting at international conferences

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship - New-Generation Control of Hybrid Wind, Solar and Battery Power Plants - DTU Wind
jobs.description:
European Doctoral Network – WindConnect | DTU Wind and Energy Systems | Fully funded · 36 months.

Shape the future of hybrid renewable power plants
Join the Renewable Power Plants (RPP) section at DTU Wind and Energy Systems and help shape the next generation of control systems for hybrid wind, solar, and battery power plants. This position is ideal for candidates with a strong interest in power systems and renewable energy integration, who are motivated by developing technical, practical solutions to complex real-world challenges and thrive in a highly international and collaborative research environment.

In this fully funded three-year PhD project, you will develop an innovative, technology-agnostic control architecture for hybrid power plants, combining advanced modelling with opportunities for experimental validation in collaboration with European Energy.

The position is part of the WindConnect European Doctoral Network, bringing together 15 PhD researchers across leading European universities and industry partners to advance the next generation of wind energy technology.

Why choose this PhD?

• Unique experimental infrastructure. In close collaboration with European Energy, you will gain hands-on exposure to DTU's MW-scale hybrid power plant research facility, one of only a few such testbeds worldwide. The facility offers opportunities to explore your control concepts in a realistic operational environment, subject to feasibility and access.
• European research community. As part of WindConnect, you will join a vibrant network of 15 doctoral researchers, collaborate with leading academic and industry partners across Europe, and undertake 6-9 months of research stays at partner institutions.
• High-impact research. Your work will help hybrid renewable power plants provide reliable grid services and support the transition to power systems with higher shares of wind and solar energy, with potential implications for grid operators, plant developers, and energy policy.
• Broad career development. Benefit from technical and transferable-skills training, industrial secondments, international conference participation, peer-reviewed publications, and a strong professional network across academia and industry.
About the project
Hybrid Power Plants (HPPs), combining wind, solar PV, and battery energy storage behind a single grid connection point, are emerging as a cornerstone of future power systems. While they can provide grid services beyond the capabilities of individual technologies, coordinating assets from different vendors with varying response times and communication protocols remains a major challenge. Traditional control architectures struggle to reconcile fast local asset responses with slower plant-level actions, while communication delays and interoperability issues add further complexity.

This PhD project addresses these challenges by developing a two-layer, technology-agnostic control architecture for utility-scale HPPs. The architecture is designed to improve interoperability, reduce communication overhead, and enhance the reliability and performance of hybrid power plants.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your research will focus on developing a two-layer, technology-agnostic control architecture for utility-scale hybrid power plants (HPPs) integrating wind, solar PV, and battery storage. The architecture will enable direct communication between the HPP controller and individual asset controllers while addressing interoperability challenges across technologies and vendors. You will design control solutions that coordinate fast local responses with plant-level objectives. The work will combine controller design, high-fidelity modelling and simulation, and, where feasible, experimental evaluation in collaboration with European Energy.

Your primary tasks will be to:

• Model and benchmark state-of-the-art HPP control architectures, including dynamic behaviour and grid-service performance.
• Identify interoperability, communication, and coordination challenges across assets, vendors, and control layers.
• Design and implement a two-layer controller that connects fast local responses with plant-wide coordination.
• Evaluate the proposed architecture using high-fidelity modelling and simulation (e.g. MATLAB/Simulink and Python) and, where feasible, explore experimental testing at DTU's hybrid power plant facility.
• Publish findings in peer-reviewed journals, present at international conferences, and contribute to IEA Wind Task 50 on Hybrid Power Plants.
• Participate in WindConnect training activities and provide limited support for MSc supervision and teaching at DTU.
What we are looking for

Essential qualifications

• MSc degree (120 ECTS or equivalent) in electrical engineering, power system engineering, control engineering, or a related field.
• Sound fundamentals in power-system dynamics and control, with an understanding of converter-interfaced generation and storage.
• Experience with dynamic modelling and simulation using tools such as MATLAB/Simulink, Python, DIgSILENT PowerFactory, PSCAD or comparable software.
• Strong analytical and research skills, with the ability to conduct independent research
Advantageous (nice to have qualifications)

• Familiarity with grid integration requirements, ancillary service provision, and/or multi-vendor renewable power plant control.
• Experience in international or cross-disciplinary research collaborations.
• Strong English communication and interpersonal skills for effective collaboration in international and multidisciplinary teams.
What we offer

• A fully funded 3-year PhD position at DTU, offering co-supervision by experienced researchers and close collaboration with European Energy and leading industry partners in an internationally recognised research environment.
• A collegial, diverse, and inclusive research environment that invests in your development, well-being, and career growth through international networking, multidisciplinary collaboration, leadership training, and partnerships with leading universities and industry across Europe.
• Diversity, equity, and inclusion. We are committed to an equitable and inclusive research environment and strongly encourage applications from women and candidates from groups underrepresented in engineering and energy research. We value curiosity, motivation, and collaboration and welcome diverse career paths and backgrounds. 
MSCA eligibility – please check before applying

This position is funded through the Marie Sklodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) European Doctoral Network. To be eligible, applicants must:

• Not hold a doctoral degree at the time of recruitment.
• Have less than four years of full-time equivalent research experience after obtaining the degree that qualifies them for PhD studies.
• Not have resided or carried out their main activity (work or studies) in Denmark for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding the recruitment date.
Please note: Applicants who do not meet these MSCA eligibility criteria cannot be considered for the position, regardless of their qualifications. Please verify your eligibility before applying. 

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

What we offer

• A fully funded 3-year PhD position at DTU, offering co-supervision by experienced researchers and close collaboration with European Energy and leading industry partners in an internationally recognised research environment.
• A collegial, diverse, and inclusive research environment that invests in your development, well-being, and career growth through international networking, multidisciplinary collaboration, leadership training, and partnerships with leading universities and industry across Europe.
• Diversity, equity, and inclusion. We are committed to an equitable and inclusive research environment and strongly encourage applications from women and candidates from groups underrepresented in engineering and energy research. We value curiosity, motivation, and collaboration and welcome diverse career paths and backgrounds.
Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The period of employment is 3 years.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
Further information may be obtained from Associate Professor Anca D. Hansen (anca@dtu.dk), Associate Professor Kaushik Das (kdas@dtu.dk) and Head of Section Gregor Giebel (grgi@dtu.dk). 

You can read more at wind.dtu.dk.

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 22 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). 

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• A 1-page research statement, including figures and references if deemed necessary (max 500 words). Research achievements (if any), methodological approaches and research objectives relevant to the framework of the PhD study are recommended elements to be included. 
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Wind and Energy Systems has led wind energy research, teaching, and commercial activities since the 1970s. With approximately 400 staff, it is the world's largest public research institute dedicated to wind and energy systems transition. Internationally recognized for pioneering wind technology and smart energy systems, the department is structured into four divisions: Materials and Components, Wind Turbine Technology, Wind Energy Systems, and Power and Energy Systems. In close collaboration with industry and public authorities, DTU Wind and Energy Systems develops cutting-edge solutions for a sustainable energy future and trains the next generation of engineers. 

About the Division: The Wind Energy Systems division focuses the development of a chain of systems that connects Atmosphere-Plant-Grid-Society. The division is home to several large software projects and datasets that help to disseminate this research to the industry and public.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: One or more Professors in Cyber Security
jobs.description:
The Department of Electronic Systems at The Technical Faculty of IT and Design invites applications for one or more professors in the field of Cyber Security as per March 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The positions are permanent.

**Who we are

**In electronic engineering, Aalborg University is known worldwide for its high academic quality and societal impact. The Department of Electronic Systems is ranked among the top 50 in the world in the Shanghai Ranking (GRAS). The department employs more than 200 people, of whom approximately 90 are PhD students, and around 40% of all employees are international. In total, the department has more than 800 students enrolled in its BSc and MSc programmes, which are based on AAU's problem-based learning model. The department leverages its unique research infrastructure and laboratory facilities to conduct world-leading fundamental and applied research within communication, networks, control systems, AI, sound, cyber security, and robotics. The department plays an active role in transferring inventions and research results into applications in close collaboration with industrial partners worldwide. You can read more about the department here www.es.aau.dk.

The Cyber Security Research Group at Aalborg University (Cyber Security Research Group) is a young and growing research group within the Department of Electronic Systems, focusing on cyber security from various perspectives. Its core research areas are network security, IoT/OT security, applied cryptography, and privacy and security in machine learning. The Cyber Security Research Group consists of 16 members and offers a young, international research environment. The group is responsible for teaching activities in the Master’s programme in Cyber Security, which is taught in English and has more than 100 active Danish and international students. Moreover, the group is strongly engaged in community-building activities, with the AAU Copenhagen campus serving as a hub for weekly CTFs and ethical hacking activities involving dozens of participants.

Your work tasks

You will lead the academic direction of cyber security research and education. The role combines independent academic leadership with close collaboration across the department, within the section, with other research environments, external organisations, and international partners.

Your research and teaching will address one or more areas within applied cryptography, IoT and/or cloud security, security and privacy for big data and machine learning, risk management and threat modelling, mobile security, secure software development, and systems security and privacy. You will initiate and lead research projects, secure and manage external research funding, publish research at an international level, and develop collaborations with industry, public-sector organisations, and universities in Denmark and abroad.

You will teach and supervise students at bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral levels, develop courses and teaching materials, and contribute to the planning and coordination of programmes built on problem-based learning. You will also supervise doctoral researchers and early-career colleagues, contribute to relevant committees and academic activities, and take part in developing the department’s research and educational priorities. International collaboration, including participation in networks, conferences, and joint research activities, forms an integral part of the position.

Your competencies

You hold a doctoral degree in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering, or a closely related field. You have documented original research contributions at an international level within cyber security and a strong publication record in recognised journals and conferences. You can demonstrate a proven track record of attracting, establishing, and managing externally funded research activities, and you have the academic judgement required to develop a coherent research agenda with clear societal and technological relevance.

You bring substantial experience in university teaching, supervision, course development, examination activities, and the development of educational programmes. Familiarity with problem-based learning is relevant, particularly because the role includes contributing to programmes in which students work collaboratively on complex and practice-oriented challenges. You communicate confidently in English, both orally and in writing, and you are willing to develop Danish language skills over time.

You set a clear academic direction while creating constructive working relationships with students, colleagues, and collaborators. You contribute with sound judgement, curiosity, and an ability to turn research ideas into well-organised projects and partnerships. You support the development of early-career researchers, engage openly across disciplines, and help maintain a respectful and collaborative research culture.

**Qualification requirements

**Applicants must be able to document a high degree of original academic production at an international level and experience from teaching at different levels. Including tests/exams, course/study programme management as well as contributions to the development of teaching activities and teaching material.

Emphasis is placed on the extent, to which the applicant, has developed the academic discipline from a research and teaching perspective.

Emphasis may moreover be placed on the applicant’s ability to carry out and develop research-based public-sector consultancy. Also, emphasis will be placed on an assessment of the applicant’s ability to perform research and teaching management tasks and possibly fulfil other functions, for example in relation to the university’s external cooperation.

Emphasis will also be placed on the applicant's ability to undertake pedagogical supervision, supervision and academic assessment work.

How to apply

Your application must include the following:

• Application, stating reasons for applying, qualifications in relation to the position, and intentions and visions for the position

• Curriculum Vitae (CV)

• Diplomas (master's degree diploma and PhD diploma)

• List of publications, with an indication of the attached publications that you wish to be taken into account in the assessment. You may attach a maximum of ten publications.

• Documentation of teaching qualifications. Please see guidelines for teaching portfolio at The Technical Faculty of IT and Design. If this is not enclosed, the applicant must enclose the reasons for this .

• Dissemination qualifications, including participation on committees or boards, participation in organisations etc.

• Additional qualifications in relation to the position

• References/recommendations

You can read more about the requirements for your application here.

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website.

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position.

Aalborg University has a policy of parallel language use. Senior Authorised Person (SAP) – Electrical Operations / Switching Leader

Location: Denmark
Employment type: Full-time
Employer: Global Nordics 

Job Description

We are seeking an experienced Senior Authorised Person (SAP) / Switching Leader (Koblingsleder) to support electrical operations on a major engineering project in Denmark.

The successful candidate will be responsible for coordinating safe switching operations, electrical isolations and safety procedures across high-voltage (HV) and low-voltage (LV) electrical systems.

The position operates within an established electrical safety management structure, under the designated Operation Manager (Driftsansvarlig Person), and in accordance with applicable Danish electrical safety regulations and EN 50110-1.

Key Responsibilities

• 
Plan, coordinate and oversee HV and LV switching operations.

• 
Prepare and review switching schedules and electrical safety documentation.

• 
Coordinate electrical isolations, earthing and safe access procedures.

• 
Prepare, issue and cancel safety documents within the scope of assigned authorisation.

• 
Coordinate with Control Engineers and electrical work teams during operational activities.

• 
Ensure appropriate safety precautions are implemented before electrical work begins.

• 
Supervise and coordinate personnel involved in electrical operational activities.

• 
Support commissioning, energisation and electrical system handover.

• 
Maintain accurate switching records, operational logs and safety documentation.

• 
Participate in safety audits, risk assessments and toolbox talks.

• 
Ensure compliance with site-specific electrical safety procedures and applicable Danish regulations.

Qualifications and Experience

• 
Relevant qualification in electrical engineering or equivalent professional experience.

• 
Extensive experience working with HV and LV electrical systems.

• 
Previous experience as a Senior Authorised Person, Switching Leader, Control Engineer or equivalent.

• 
Strong understanding of electrical switching, isolation, earthing and safe working procedures.

• 
Knowledge of EN 50110-1 and electrical safety management systems.

• 
Experience preparing switching schedules and electrical safety documentation.

• 
Demonstrated ability to coordinate electrical work teams and operational activities.

• 
Strong communication, organisational and safety leadership skills.

• 
Good command of English.

Electrical Safety Requirements

The successful candidate will undergo a competence assessment and receive the necessary written operational appointment and authorisation under the project's Danish electrical safety management arrangements (KLS-D) before undertaking regulated electrical activities.

The role does not include statutory Operation Manager responsibilities or electrical installation work requiring separate company authorisation.

Application

Please submit your CV, relevant qualifications and details of your professional experience.
